newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO CRIMINALISE RACKETEERING, TAX EVASION.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO CRIMINALISE RACKETEERING, TAX EVASION.

text.p: New laws prepared by Bulgaria's interior ministry will criminalise racketeering and tax evasion which have soared since the collapse of communist rule in 1989, the interior ministry said on Tuesday.

"Under the amendments to the criminal code, which are yet to be approved by the cabinet and passed in the parliament, racketeering and evading taxes are considered as a crime," ministry secretary Atanas Atanasov told a news conference.
He said that Bulgaria urgently needed to update its legislation. Before 1989, all workers were employed by the state and most taxes were deducted at source.

"The proposed amendments envisage up to seven years imprisonment for racketeering and between five and 15 years in case of violence or if the racketeering has been ordered by a criminal economic group," Atanasov said.
Many former sportsmen whose careers ended with the fall of communism now use their brawn in the service of private security firms and insurance companies.
Atanasov said a jail term of up to three years was envisaged for evasion of taxes above two million levs.
The Union of Democratic Forces which won a big majority in the Saturday's general election said on Monday that fighting crime would be a top priority of the future UDF cabinet.
